resources.string: Keeps you out of the Instagram Reels feed.

InstaFocus reads the names of on-screen views inside the Instagram app (for example \"reel viewer\" or \"Reels tab\") to notice when the Reels feed opens, then taps Home or Back for you. It does not read messages, captions or usernames, and nothing is stored or sent anywhere: the app has no internet permission.
The accessibility service is not enabled. Open Accessibility settings and turn on InstaFocus.
The service is enabled but not connected. Toggle it off and on again, and set InstaFocus to Never sleeping in battery settings.
The Reels feed is blocked in Instagram.
The service is running but Block Reels is off.
Allow single shared reel (DMs, Explore, feed)
Play the one reel you opened, but snap back if you swipe to the next.

If the InstaFocus switch is greyed out in Accessibility settings, Android has restricted it because the app was not installed from a store. Open App info, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, choose Allow restricted settings, confirm, then go back and enable the service.
Samsung phones may stop the service in the background. In Settings > Battery > Background usage limits, add InstaFocus to Never sleeping apps (or open App info > Battery and choose Unrestricted).

InstaFocus looks at Instagram\'s view ids, not at what is on the screen. When the full-screen reel viewer appears from the Reels tab, it taps Home. When you open a reel from a DM, Explore or the feed, that one reel plays; swiping to the next one scrolls you back. It reacts after the viewer appears, so a frame or two of a reel may flash. It depends on Instagram\'s internal names, so an Instagram update can break it until the rules are updated. It never acts when it is unsure, so it will rather miss a reel than block a chat.
Keeps the ids of the views on screen in the last scan, in memory only. No text, names or messages.
No entries yet. Open Instagram with the service running.
